title: parametrize-observability-alert-templates-and-add-rollback-playbook
author: Priya Bhandari
release_notes: Introduce parameterized Prometheus alert templates (tenant, severity, threshold overrides) and add an operator-friendly rollback playbook + Helm hooks for safe upgrades.
description:
Motivation: Private installs run in heterogenous environments with differing tenant scales and alerting tolerances. Current hard-coded alert rules caused frequent noisy paging for customers with low-volume deployments and required manual edits during upgrades. This PR parameterizes alert templates, surfaces a compact variables schema to the installer, and introduces a tested rollback playbook and Helm upgrade hooks to make observability upgrades safe and reversible.

Summary of changes (single-line description string with sections, commits and files):
- Templates: Move prometheus alert rules to templated YAML under charts/observability/templates/alerts.tpl and charts/observability/values.alerts.yaml. Templates accept variables: tenant_scope, cpu_high_threshold, memory_high_threshold, alert_ttl, mute_on_scale_down.
- Helm: Update Chart.yaml and values schema (values.schema.json) to validate alert parameter types and introduce .Files.Get-based include for generated rules. Add pre-upgrade hook that snapshots current ConfigMaps and a post-failure hook that triggers the rollback job.
- Terraform: Add new module observability/terraform/alerting_vars.tf and an outputs.tf to expose the evaluated alert_config to downstream modules (so Private Installer can compute conservative defaults per deployment).
- Docs/playbook: Add docs/ops/observability_rollback_playbook.md describing step-by-step manual rollback, automated rollback-runbook.sh, and a small acceptance test harness under test/integration/observability_rollback_test.sh.
- CI: Add a lightweight lint + helm template render job to nightly pipeline for private-installer.

Small snippet to illustrate template variable usage (kept short):
{{"{{ if eq .Values.alerts.tenant_scope \"global\" }}"}}
- alert: HighCPULoad
  expr: sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m])) by (pod) > {{"{{ .Values.alerts.cpu_high_threshold }}"}}
  for: {{"{{ .Values.alerts.alert_ttl }}"}}
{{"{{ end }}"}}

Upgrade / rollout guidance (short):
- Default behavior: installer keeps previous alert ConfigMaps intact during helm upgrade; new templated rules are applied only after a successful post-install validation probe.
- If the post-install probe fails, the post-failure hook triggers rollback job: it replaces the active ConfigMaps with the snapshot taken by pre-upgrade hook, and emits an event to the operator with a link to the rollback playbook.
- Operators can run docs/ops/observability_rollback_playbook.md for manual remediation; automated script rollback-runbook.sh is idempotent and exits non-zero on unresolved drift.

Testing performed:
- Local kind cluster: full Helm upgrade + forced failure scenario (post-failure hook exercised).
- Integration CI: helm template rendering against values permutations (tenant_scope="global", tenant_scope="per-tenant", low/high thresholds).
- Terraform module: unit test for alert_config output mapping.

Backward compatibility: Templates default to previous rule semantics if no alert overrides are supplied. Terraform change is additive (new outputs) but customers pinning old module versions must add the new output mapping. This is documented in the release notes.

Operational impact & mitigations:
- Intended to reduce noisy paging for small deployments and provide safe path for observability upgrades.
- Added feature flags under values.alerts.enable_parametrization to opt-out for customers who want manual control.

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main after all approvals (merge method: squash). Release: included in private-installer v1.18.0 (observability patch).

Notes for on-call / SRE: The rollback job emits metrics under redwood_private_installer.rollback.* and events are logged to the audit log path: /var/log/redwood-installer/rollback-events.log. The playbook maps common failure signatures (CRD validation, missing RBAC for ConfigMap updates) to recommended fixes.
